examples.code:
<DataTable
  caption="Mitglieder"
  columns={[{ id: 'name', header: 'Name', sortable: true, isRowHeader: true }]}
  data={[
    { id: 'm1', name: 'Emmy Noether' },
    { id: 'm2', name: 'Lise Meitner' },
    { id: 'm3', name: 'Konrad Zuse' },
  ]}
  selectionMode="multiple"
  hasSearch
  pageSize={2}
  isFullwidth
  labels={{
    selectAll: 'Alle Zeilen dieser Seite auswählen',
    selectRow: label => `${label} auswählen`,
    sortHint: 'Spaltenköpfe mit Schaltflächen sind sortierbar',
    search: 'Suchen',
    results: count => (count === 1 ? '1 Treffer' : `${count} Treffer`),
    pageRange: (first, last, total) => `${first} bis ${last} von ${total}`,
    loading: 'Wird geladen',
    pagination: 'Mitglieder, Seiten',
    empty: 'Noch keine Mitglieder.',
    noResults: 'Keine Treffer.',
  }}
/>

accessibility:
- **A native table,** as in the ARIA Authoring Practices' Sortable Table example: `th scope="col"`
  headers, `th scope="row"` for the row header, and a `caption` or your `aria-label` or
  `aria-labelledby` as its name. A development build warns when it has none.
- **Sorting:** a sortable header holds a `<button>` with the header's text, and only the sorted
  header has `aria-sort`, `ascending` or `descending`, which screen readers read out as they reach
  it. That headers with buttons sort is said once, hidden at the end of the caption, or as a hidden
  caption of its own when `aria-label` names the table. The indicator is drawn in CSS, so it's not
  read.
- **Selection** rides on the checkboxes: each is named "Select" and the row's label, and the one in
  the header is mixed (`aria-checked="mixed"`) when some of the page is selected. Rows get Bulma's
  selected look and no `aria-selected`, which ARIA gives the rows of a grid rather than a table.
- **A status message** in a polite live region says how many rows match a short while after the
  search or a filter changes, the range shown after a page change, and "Loading" while `loading` is
  on after one of those. Nothing is said as the page loads, or for a sort, which `aria-sort` covers.
- **The pager** is a `navigation` named after the table, so two tables on a page have two named
  pagers.
- **Busy:** `aria-busy` is on the table while `loading`, and the skeleton rows are hidden from
  assistive tech.
- **Wide tables:** with `isResponsive`, the `ScrollArea` around the table is a tab stop and a
  named region while it overflows, so it can be scrolled from the keyboard.
- **Forced colors:** the sort indicator is painted in the system's button text color, and the sort
  button's focus ring is an outline. A selected row's fill is a color forced colors takes away, so
  the checked checkbox carries the selection there.
- **No motion:** nothing animates but the skeleton, which stops under reduced motion.
summary: The `DataTable` component is a table of records that people can sort, search, page through and select rows from, rendered with bestax's own `Table` parts, `Checkbox` and `Pagination`. It's a native table, as in the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices' sortable table: a sortable header holds a button, the sorted one carries `aria-sort`, and each row's checkbox is named for the row. It runs on `useDataTable`, which custom markup can use too.

parts.summary: The `DataTable` component is a table of records that people can sort, search, page through and select rows from, rendered with bestax's own `Table` parts, `Checkbox` and `Pagination`. It's a native table, as in the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices' sortable table: a sortable header holds a button, the sorted one carries `aria-sort`, and each row's checkbox is named for the row. It runs on `useDataTable`, which custom markup can use too.

props.name: columns
props.description: The columns, in the order they're shown. Required unless `table` is given. Keep the array the same from one render to the next, defined outside the component or in `useMemo`: a new one has every cell's text worked out again.

props.name: data
props.description: The rows, as records of your own. Required unless `table` is given.

props.name: table
props.description: A table made by `useDataTable`, rendered in place of one made from `columns`, `data` and the state props, which are then left unread. Use it to put a toolbar, a count or an export button elsewhere on the page.

props.name: caption
props.description: Names the table, as a visible `<caption>`. A table needs a name: this, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

props.name: isBordered
props.description: Adds borders to all cells.

props.name: isStriped
props.description: Adds zebra-striping to rows.

props.name: isNarrow
props.description: Makes the table more compact by cutting cell padding in half.

props.name: isHoverable
props.description: Adds a hover effect on rows.

props.name: isFullwidth
props.description: Makes the table span the full width of its wrapper.

props.name: isResponsive
props.description: Scrolls a table wider than its wrapper sideways, in a `ScrollArea` named after the table, which can be scrolled from the keyboard while it overflows.

props.name: hasSearch
props.description: Shows a search field in the toolbar, labelled by `labels.search`.

props.name: toolbar
props.description: More of the toolbar, after the search field: buttons for the selected rows, a filter, a download. Given the table.

props.name: loading
props.description: Shows a page of skeleton rows under the header in place of the rows, and marks the table busy. For data on its way, as from a server with `manual`.

props.name: empty
props.description: What the table shows when it has no rows at all, in one cell across every column. A small `EmptyState` saying `labels.empty` by default. A title of your own sits under the heading the table does, so give it the next level down with `titleAs`.

props.name: noResults
props.description: What the table shows when the search and filters let no row through, in one cell across every column. A small `EmptyState` saying `labels.noResults` by default. A button that clears the search goes away with it, so send focus back to the search field when it's pressed.

props.name: rowProps
props.description: Props of your own for a row's `Tr`, such as a handler or a class. The table's own (`isSelected`) win. To wrap a row in a `ContextMenu`, build the table from `useDataTable`'s props instead.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes, on the wrapper `<div>`.

props.name: getRowId
props.description: A row's id, unique and stable, which the selection is a list of. Left out, it's the row's `id` property as a string. A development build warns about a missing or repeated id, and a row with none falls back to its index, which doesn't survive the data changing.

props.name: sort
props.description: The sort when you hold it: an array of `{ id, direction }`, the first deciding and each next one breaking ties. The headers set one at a time.

props.name: defaultSort
props.description: The sort to start with when the table holds it. Text sorts in the `LocaleProvider`'s locale, or the runtime's own outside one, which can differ between a server and the browser, so put a table rendered on the server sorted inside a `LocaleProvider`.

props.name: onSortChange
props.description: Called with the new sort when a header is pressed.

props.name: selectionMode
props.description: `multiple` adds a checkbox to each row and a "select all" checkbox to the header.

props.name: selected
props.description: The selected rows' ids when you hold them. They stay selected while the search, a filter or the page hides them.

props.name: defaultSelected
props.description: The rows selected to begin with, by id, when the table holds them.

props.name: onSelectedChange
props.description: Called with every selected id after a checkbox changes.

props.name: pageSize
props.description: Rows per page. Set, the table pages through `Pagination`; left out, it shows every row.

props.name: page
props.description: The page shown when you hold it, counting from 1. A page past the end shows the last.

props.name: defaultPage
props.description: The page to start on when the table holds it.

props.name: onPageChange
props.description: Called with the page chosen in the pager, and with 1 when the search or a filter changes through the table while the page held isn't 1, even when a page past the end shows as the last.

props.name: search
props.description: The search when you hold it, matched against every filterable column's text: in the `LocaleProvider`'s locale, ignoring case and the accents the language ignores, or a case-insensitive substring outside one.

props.name: defaultSearch
props.description: The search to start with when the table holds it.

props.name: onSearchChange
props.description: Called with the search as it changes through the table.

props.name: filters
props.description: A value per column, by `id`, when you hold them. A row passes when every column with a value passes it: the column's `filterFn` if it has one, given the value as it is, or else the column's text has to contain the value's text, compared as the search compares. An array is a choice of values, as a multiple-choice filter gives, and passes a row whose text contains any of them. A value of `undefined`, `null`, `''` or an empty array is no filter.

props.name: defaultFilters
props.description: The filters to start with when the table holds them.

props.name: onFiltersChange
props.description: Called with every filter value after one changes through the table.

props.name: manual
props.description: Hands sorting, filtering and paging to a server: the table shows `data` as given, as the current page, and only reports the state as it changes.

props.name: rowCount
props.description: With `manual`, how many rows match in all, which sets the page count and the announced count. Without it, the table counts the rows in `data`, which with a `pageSize` is one page and no pager, and a development build warns.

props.name: labels
props.description: The words the table writes, in your app's language.

extraProps.name: aria-label
extraProps.description: Names the table, in place of a `caption`. A table needs a name, so pass a `caption`, this or `aria-labelledby`, and a development build warns when it has none.

extraProps.name: aria-labelledby
extraProps.description: The id of a visible heading that names the table, in place of a `caption`.
